selected.name: 01-existing-data
selected.prompt: Draw one sparse hand-drawn scene explaining that a grocery data platform ALREADY contains work from many teams. Landscape 3:2, ivory #fffdf7, loose charcoal fineliner lines, tiny muted red data dots, no shading, no decoration, no polished vector shapes. Across the top/upper middle place FIVE simple small source doodles, with generous spacing: receipt labelled 'Purchases'; barcode/product tag labelled 'Products'; farm/fishery pin sheet labelled 'Origins'; two pins joined by a road labelled 'Journeys'; food-label slip with a small apple labelled 'Nutrition'. These are different operational systems and teams, not five fields on one form. Small thin lines carrying red dots converge into ONE open shared notebook below, with a few short ruled rows and no tiny data text. Near each source a tiny simple human bust suggests a different owning team, no detailed faces. No trucks or busy scenery, no database architecture boxes, no new ingestion/setup instructions, no claims of complete provenance. The idea is many teams' everyday work creating a shared foundation before a product manager starts querying. Only the five labels requested; no extra title or captions.

selected.name: 02-explore-own-data
selected.prompt: Create one separate minimal hand-drawn pen illustration for a blog. Landscape 3:2, plain very light warm ivory paper #fffdf7, loose imperfect charcoal fineliner strokes and tiny muted red data dots. Sparse science-whiteboard explainer, plenty of empty margins, no shading or scenery, no architecture boxes, no professional vector polish, no logos. Show a curious product manager at a laptop, exploring THEIR OWN grocery purchase history with a small friendly agent doodle alongside. Three groups at most: expressive person, laptop, small agent. The person's simple face has exaggerated raised eyebrows, a long amusing nose, inquisitive wide eyes and a slightly surprised half smile, original character not a portrait. The laptop display has only the handwritten title 'My purchases', a little fish and carrot row, and a few short scribbles. The agent holds a tiny paper labelled 'SQL'. One small speech bubble from the person asks exactly 'What do I buy most?'. A second tiny thought doodle with a location pin and question mark suggests looking up origins. No made-up totals or countries, no complete SQL, no data-platform diagrams. They are playfully finding meaningful and fun statistics in existing data, not configuring ingestion. Keep everything very simple and clearly readable.

selected.name: 03-connect-the-data

A minimal analyst's investigation without a person: on the left a loosely drawn receipt item showing a tiny fish and the short handwritten identifiers 'item' and 'batch'. In the centre a large simple magnifying glass over a red dotted connection; one gap in the dotted line ends in a small question mark, showing that not every purchase has traceable origin. selected.name: 04-reused-models
selected.prompt: One separate sparse hand-drawn sketch about shared SQL models feeding a grocery annual recap. Landscape 3:2, ivory #fffdf7 paper, loose imperfect charcoal fineliner, tiny muted red data dots, lots of whitespace, no shading, no architecture boxes or polished vector graphics. Draw a loose SQL recipe sheet on the left labelled 'purchase items'. From it thin hand-drawn lines carry red data dots to THREE smaller recipe slips in a loose middle column, labelled 'item origins', 'item journeys', 'item nutrition'. Tiny side-input doodles of a farm pin, route pins, and food label feed the corresponding middle slips, indicating that different teams maintain those shared inputs. The THREE middle model results converge into one loose sheet on the right labelled 'yearly recap'. Show 'SQL' at the top of each recipe, two scribbled lines only, no actual SQL and no quantities. Clearly show one shared model being REUSED by several later models and their results combined, not disconnected dashboards or raw data being repeatedly fetched. No people, phones, logos or captions. This is a modest conceptual teaching sketch, not a promise that every purchase has all provenance recorded.
